chats.typed: which nas runs on 12 v in a van or rv and how much power does it draw
queries: Synology DS223j power supply 12V watt consumption access hibernation official; QNAP TS-233 12V power consumption official; TerraMaster F2-223 12V power consumption official
chats.answer:
For a van or RV, I recommend a NAS that runs directly from 12V DC, rather than a conventional NAS that needs 120V AC through an inverter.

The main things to consider are:

Power consumption: Ideally 5–15W at idle and under 30W during normal operation.

Input voltage: A van's 12V electrical system can range from roughly 11–14.6V, so a regulated 12V supply is important.

Storage: SSDs are preferable to spinning hard drives because they use less power and tolerate vibration better.

Battery life: Every 12W of continuous consumption uses 288Wh per day.

A NAS drawing 10W continuously uses only 240Wh per day, while a 40W NAS consumes 960Wh per day — a substantial difference when running off batteries.

How much battery will it use?

Assuming a 12.8V LiFePO4 battery, a NAS operating continuously at the indicated wattage would use approximately:

Important for RV installation

Even with a 12V NAS, don't connect it directly to an unregulated vehicle battery circuit. Use a fused, regulated 12V DC-DC converter rated for the NAS's startup and peak power. The QNAP TS-233 specifies at least a 48W power adapter, despite using only about 11W typically.

One question: Are you planning to use two SSDs, two 3.5-inch hard drives, or an all-NVMe NAS?

That makes a big difference in power consumption. For a van running on solar and batteries, an all-SSD NAS may be the best choice.
